definition: Terms/codes for describing the consequences of the medical device adverse event/incident on the person affected.
statusDescription: Please use more detailed term within the hierarchy

definition: Change in response to treatment or cure of a disorder or disease.
A reduction in or complete loss of the desirable and beneficial effects resulting from a medical treatment.
statusDescription: Definition modified for Release Number 2026. See no. 114 of Change Request Log

definition: An increase in the desirable and beneficial effects resulting from a medical treatment.
Unanticipated desirable and beneficial effects resulting from a medical treatment.
An increase in the time taken to achieve the desirable and beneficial effects resulting from a medical treatment
statusDescription: Term added for Release Number 2026. See no. 33 of Change Request Log

definition: The cessation of life.

Death in utero; failure of the product of conception to show evidence of respiration, heart beat, or definite movement of a voluntary muscle after expulsion from the uterus, with no possibility of resuscitation.
The cessation of life due to permanent loss of brain function and brainstem for absence of responsiveness to external stimuli, absence of reflex and apnea.
Patient diagnosis was clinically significant delayed as a consequence of device performance.
Patient treatment was delayed or interrupted as a consequence of device performance.
statusDescription: Definition modified for Release Number 2026. See no. 178 of Change Request Log

definition: Situation in which the use of the device impedes or affects a subsequent medical procedure or use of a medicine or device. The time elapsed between the use of the device and the medical procedure is not a factor. It is not necessary for the device to have broken or malfunctioned.
Use of the device has lead to worsening of the existing disease or condition, as a direct consequence of device use
statusDescription: Definition modified for Release Number 2026. See no. 12 of Change Request Log

definition: Hospitalization or prolonged hospitalization due to the health damage accompanying the use of device.
Patient requires admission to or extension of stay in an intensive care unit.
Patient required emergency transfer to a different facility because of the need for an additional level of care.
statusDescription: Term added for Release Number 2025. See no. 28 of Change Request Log

definition: Fetal distress, congenital physical or mental impairment or birth defect, excluding fetal death.

Patient did not receive intended treatment from a device or received inadequate treatment as a consequence of device performance. This includes inadequate/inappropriate electrical stimulation or radiation dosage during procedures.
statusDescription: Definition modified for Release Number 2025. See no. 19 of Change Request Log

definition: Patient treatment was absent as a consequence of device performance.
Receiving incorrect or incompatible whole blood or a blood component.
A dose of medicine was not taken or delivered at the prescribed dosing interval.
Exposure to, or intake of, an insufficient amount of a substance.
A lower than intended dose of radiation to a single field.
Exposure to, or intake of, an excessive amount of a substance.
A higher than intended cumulative dose of radiation to a single field.
The worsening of a disease over time due to inadequate treatment.
statusDescription: Term was added on 27 January 2022. For details, see comment No. 191 of the Change Log (Release Number 2022). Term retired for Release Number 2025. Use F1010 "Inadequate Treatment" or F30 "Disease Progression". See no. 63 of Change Request Log

term: Exposure to Contaminated Device/Risk of Infection
definition: Exposure to a non-sterile device or conditions where infection is likely.
statusDescription: Term was added on 27 January 2022. For details, see comment No. 214 of the Change Log (Release Number 2022).

definition: Unintended exposure of the patient and/or healthcare providers to drugs or other substances.  This can include any exposure routes such as skin, mucous membranes, and respiratory.
statusDescription: Term added for Release Number 2024. See no. 25 of Change Log. Formatting change to Term for Release Number 2025. See no. 21 of Change Request Log

definition: Patient received treatment which was unnecessary or excessive. This includes treatment following a false positive diagnosis and excessive stimulation or shock delivery.  For drug or radiation overdose use F1005 or child term.
statusDescription: Term added for Release Number 2025. See no. 20 of Change Request Log

definition: Patient received inadequate or insufficient treatment of an appropriate type.  This includes inadequate stimulation or shock delivery.   For inappropriate treatment use F1009. For drug or radiation underdose use F1004 or child term.
statusDescription: Term added for Release Number 2025. See no. 63 of Change Request Log

definition: A non-serious injury, illness or impairment which can be treated with minimal or no intervention, including monitoring only.
statusDescription: Definition was modified on 31 January 2023 (Old definition: A mild injury, illness or impairment which can be treated with minimal or no intervention.). For details, see comment No. 143 of the Change Log (Release Number 2023). Term and Definition modified for Release Number 2025. Previous term was "Minor Injury/ Illness / Impairment". See no. 79 of Change Request Log.

definition: A severe injury, illness or impairment which requires hospitalization or medical intervention.
Disease that persists over a long period of time, cannot be prevented by vaccines or cured by medication, nor do they just disappear.
Any physical or mental impairment that interferes with an individual's ability to perform desired activities.
Patient suffered an illness or injury which if not treated would be fatal.
Irreversible deterioration of the state of health.
Reversible deterioration of the state of health.
An incorrect diagnosis or classification of an illness or other problem.
Clinically significant extended treatment time or procedural time. Not to be used for prolonged hospitalization or prolonged surgery.
statusDescription: Editorial change to the definition on 16 February 2021.

definition: Patient experiencing a complication that is well documented in association with the device or procedure.
statusDescription: Editorial change to term for consistency for Release Number 2026. See no. 191 of Change Log.

definition: Decrease in lifetime/ lifespan of an individual. Decline in the normal duration or in average life.
Patient required sedation or additional sedation.
Patient requires treatment to facilitate the process of recovery from injury, illness, or disease.
One or more surgical procedures, including percutaneous or minimally invasive procedures, were required, or an existing procedure changed.
statusDescription: Definition was modified on 31 January 2023 (Old definition: One or more surgical procedures was required, or an existing procedure changed). For details, see comment No. 135 /137/138 /139 /140/141 of the Change Log (Release Number 2023).

definition: Surgical intervention that was not planned and needed to be performed in addition to other interventions including surgical ones.
Patient required surgical removal of limb, extremities or other external body parts.
Patient required a corrective invasive procedure to remove a device, or parts/fragments of a device.

Patient required a corrective invasive procedure in which a device was repositioned. This includes implantable, surgically invasive (penetration through the surface of the body) or invasive (penetration though a natural body orifice or permanent artificial opening, e.g. stoma) devices.

Patient required a corrective invasive procedure in which a device was replaced/revised. This includes implantable, surgically invasive (penetration through the surface of the body) or invasive (penetration though a natural body orifice or permanent artificial opening, e.g. stoma) devices.
A change of surgical procedures from the original plan.
Surgery that is more complicated, more comprehensive or more extensive than planned (e.g. percutaneous to open surgery).
statusDescription: Definition was modified on 31 January 2023 (Old definition: Patient required additional or unexpected endoscopic procedure). For details, see comment No. 139 of the Change Log (Release Number 2023).

term: Conversion from Robotic-Assisted Procedure to Other Surgical Approach
definition: A surgical procedure initially intended to be completed using robotic assistance that is converted intraoperatively to a different surgical approach. This change may result from robotic system limitations, technical issues, or surgeon preference to complete the procedure safely and effectively.
statusDescription: Term added for Release Number 2026. See no. 115 of Change Request Log.

definition: Surgery that takes longer than anticipated.
statusDescription: Formatting change to Term for Release Number 2025. See no. 21 of Change Request Log

definition: Surgical procedure unable to be completed when originally scheduled and put off until some time in the future.

Surgical procedure aborted, or unable to be completed.
This applies to cases where there is no information whether the procedure will be carried out at a later time, or where it is known that surgery will not go ahead.
If it is known that the procedure has been, or will be, carried out later then use F1909 - Surgical Procedure Delayed
statusDescription: Term added for Release Number 2024. See no. 110 of Change Log. Formatting change to Term for Release Number 2025. See no. 21 of Change Request Log. Editorial change to term for consistency for Release Number 2026. See no. 192 of Change Log.

definition: Any event type, which results in imminent risk of death, serious injury, or serious illness to more than one individual, that requires prompt remedial action.
Unexpected clinical deterioration of patient.
Diagnostic intervention needed to be completed that was not originally planned.
Patient required removal of tissue or fluid specimen to establish a diagnosis, including biopsy and blood samples.
statusDescription: Technical change to definition for Release Number 2026. See 5 of Change Log

definition: Patient required additional or unexpected endoscopic diagnostic procedure.
statusDescription: Definition was modified on 31 January 2023 (Old definition: Patient required additional or unexpected endoscopic procedure). For details, see comment No. 137 of the Change Log (Release Number 2023).

definition: Requirement for imaging that was not originally planned.
Patient required additional or unexpected IVD testing.
statusDescription: Editorial change to the definition on 16 February 2021.

definition: Patient required an unforeseen medical intervention, excluding surgery, which was not on the original treatment plan.
Use of an additional or alternative device require to achieve optimal outcome.

term: Additional Device of Same Type Required
definition: The situation where an additional device of the same type and intended purpose as the original device is required to continue or complete the intended procedure or therapy.
statusDescription: Term added for Release Number 2026. See no. 35 of Change Request Log

term: Additional Device of Different Type Required
definition: The situation where an additional device of a different type or intended purpose is required to mitigate risk or prevent harm to the patient following the use or failure of the original device. This may involve introducing a complementary or alternative device to address complications
statusDescription: Term added for Release Number 2026. See no. 35 of Change Request Log

definition: Patient required an infusion of whole blood or a blood component directly into the bloodstream.
Patient required new/additional medication or additional dose of existing medication.
A medication or course of action used to prevent a possible disease or condition from occurring.
statusDescription: Definition modified for Release Number 2025. See no. 99 of Change Request Log

definition: Patient required additional radiation therapy.
statusDescription: Editorial change to the definition on 16 February 2021.

definition: Patient required resuscitation.
Patient required programming changes to be made to an implantable or other programmable device.
statusDescription: Term was added on 31 January 2023. For details, see comment No. 133 of the Change Log (Release Number 2023).

definition: Patient required non-surgical treatment under anaesthesia.
statusDescription: Term added for Release Number 2024. See no. 111 of Change Log. Editorial change to term for consistency for Release Number 2026. See no. 310 of Change Log.

definition: Patient required ventilation or clinically significant extension of existing ventilation
statusDescription: Term added for Release Number 2025. See no. 27 of Change Request Log

definition: It is not clear whether any health impact occurred, or health impact appears to have occurred, but there is not yet enough information available to classify the health impact.
statusDescription: Definition was modified on 31 January 2023 (Old definition: There is not yet enough information available to classify the health impact). For details, see comment No. 102 of the Change Log (Release Number 2023). Term and Definition modified for Release Number 2025. Previous term was "Insufficient Information". See no. 122 of Change Request Log.

definition: Complication occurring in the patient that had not previously been identified or expected for this device.
statusDescription: Editorial change to the definition on 16 February 2021.

definition: No apparent harm occurred in relation to the adverse event.
statusDescription: Editorial change to the definition on 16 February 2021.
Term added for Release Number 2024. See no. 120 of Change Log. Editorial change to term for consistency for Release Number 2026. See no. 311 of Change Log.

Term and Definition modified for Release Number 2024. Previous term was No Patient Involvement. See no. 121 of Change Log. Editorial change to term for consistency for Release Number 2026. See no. 312 of Change Log.

term: Appropriate Health Impact Term/Code not Available
definition: The Health Impact is not adequately described by any other term. Note: this code must not be used unless there is no other feasible code. The preferred term should be documented when submitting an adverse event report. This information will be used to determine if a new term should be added to the code table.
statusDescription: Term and Definition modified for Release Number 2025. Previous term was "Appropriate Term/Code Not Available". See no. 111 of Change Request Log. Editorial change to term for consistency for Release Number 2026. See no. 313 of Change Log.

term: Death not Related to Reported Adverse Event
definition: A death has occurred, but it was confirmed that the event did not contribute to the death.  Other terms may also be selected if it is possible to link the adverse event to other identifiable health impacts.
statusDescription: Term added for Release Number 2024. See no. 119 of Change Log. Editorial change to term for consistency for Release Number 2026. See no. 314 of Change Log.

definition: The worsening of a disease over time related to device performance (e.g. insufficient therapeutic effect, delayed action).
statusDescription: Definition modified for Release Number 2026. See no. 13 of Change Request Log

definition: Patient treatment aborted, or unable to be completed. This applies to cases where there is no information whether the treatment will be carried out at a later time, or where it is known that treatment will not go ahead. If it is known that the treatment has been, or will be, carried out later then use F05 - Delay to Treatment/ Therapy
statusDescription: Term added for Release Number 2025. See no. 84 of Change Request Log. Editorial change to term for consistency for Release Number 2026. See no. 193 of Change Log.
